CHIEF COMPLAINT: Mild lower back pain for 3 days after gardening.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 40-year-old presents with dull lower back pain that began after heavy gardening over the weekend. No radiation to legs, no numbness or weakness.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Negative for fever, numbness, weakness, bowel or bladder changes. Positive for localized back pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: No chronic conditions, no prior back injuries.

VITALS: BP 120/78, HR 68, Temp 98.2F, RR 14.

PHYSICAL EXAM: Lumbar paraspinal tenderness without midline tenderness, straight leg raise negative bilaterally, normal strength and sensation in lower extremities.

ASSESSMENT: Acute mechanical lower back strain.

PLAN: NSAIDs as needed, activity modification, heat therapy, follow up in 2 weeks if not improved.
